newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-PAKISTAN HIT BACK IN SECOND TEST.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PAKISTAN HIT BACK IN SECOND TEST.

text.p: Pakistan fought back strongly in the afternoon session to claim five Sri Lankan wickets and put their hosts on the defensive on the first day of the second and final test match on Saturday.
Sri Lanka, who went to lunch at 94-0, crashed to 167 for 5 at tea as the Pakistani spin duo of Saqlain Mushtaq and Mushtaq Ahmed got to work.
The first to go soon after lunch was Sanath Jayasuriya who added only one run to his interval score of 71 before being caught by Mushtaq at first slip attempting to cut Saqlain.

Maravan Atapattu quickly followed, caught at silly point for 14, before Russell Arnold, who shared a highest first wicket partnership against Pakistan with Jayasuriya, was run out after being called for a sharp single by Aravinda De Silva. Arnold batted for 183 minutes for his 37, which included four boundaries.

Saqlain then took the prize wicket of captain Arjuna Ranatunga for four to leave Sri Lanka tottering, and their position worsened when Hashan Tillekeratne was bowled by a quick delivery from paceman Mohammed Zahid when he had scored 10.
De Silva, who had reached 20 not out, and Romesh Kaluwitharana then took Sri Lanka to tea without further loss.
Scores: Sri Lanka 167 for 5 at tea (S.Jayasuriya 72, Saqlain Mushtaq 2 for 58).
